provenance.authorAccess: Scenario author did not read source implementation, v1 cases, predictions, annotations, or evaluation reports.
provenance.method: 240 separately written pair narratives across 12 procurement families; a deterministic serializer supplies record IDs, synthetic document hashes and asynchronous entry timestamps.
provenance.documents: Receipt hashes represent fictional uploaded files, not reconstructed source documents. Shared files may contain multiple payable lines. Different hashes may represent copies, rescans, corrected forms, or different documents.
provenance.scope: Scenario narratives can include operational facts unavailable in predictor records. No supplier identity or receipt line allocation is added to the persisted record schema.
provenance.annotationStatus: Unannotated. No author decision key, evidence-tier key, prediction, or model score is included.
limitations: Fictional narratives and common author conventions are not operational prevalence evidence.
Transaction histories can remain unresolved; narratives intentionally do not guarantee binary certainty.
Creation timestamps are synthetic entry times and must not be read as service dates.

annotationMethod.method: Two fresh independent model-blind nonexpert AI judgments per case; blind to scoring, predictions, split/family/category and author target answers. Any identity disagreement merges to ambiguous; any tier disagreement merges to ambiguous. No prediction-based adjudication. Raw judgments retained.

splitPolicy.groupIsolation: Each procurement dossier has a unique groupId; no family or group appears in both splits.
splitPolicy.annotationProtocol: Separate blind reviewers receive shuffled id/scenario/left/right packets only; category, split and supplyFamily are withheld.

metricsInterpretation: Calibration only; no heldout performance claim.
limitations: New fictional synthetic pairs with nonexpert model-blind AI annotations, subjective confidence and retained ambiguity; not real-field or human-adjudicated truth.
Binary transaction identity and independently annotated records-only evidence tiers are different targets. Scenario-only facts are unavailable to either predictor.
Few supply-family clusters and common author templates make paired bootstrap intervals exploratory. Case-level Wilson intervals ignore cluster dependence.
Balanced synthetic sampling does not estimate real prevalence, operational workload or fraud probability. All tiers remain advisory; no approval, rejection or payment action occurs.
The fixed 20% global pair budget is a bounded surrogate, not a multi-candidate retrieval benchmark; no MAP/NDCG claim. Workload counts are not human minutes.

Application risk API supplies at most 100 candidates, currently truncates stored candidates in storage order before revised tier ranking. This pairwise evaluator supplies one candidate and has no candidate truncation; global ranking has deterministic case-ID ties.
Methods share genuine pinned local CPU embeddings. Per-method scoring excludes shared model work. Host timing does not establish browser/mobile performance.
